stages.name: Unauthenticated RCE via Web Vulnerabilities
observables: XML external entity (XXE) payloads in HTTP requests
OGNL injection strings in web parameters
Path traversal sequences (../) in file-repository upload paths
Administrator viewing malicious MMS3 patch metadata

stages.name: Local Privilege Escalation to Root
observables: Modification of nable-writable syslog-ng configuration files
nable service account spawning shell with root privileges

observables: New local user accounts created on the N-central appliance

scenario.summary: The Able2Shell disclosure identifies 33 vulnerabilities in the N-able N-central RMM platform, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via XXE, OGNL injection, and path traversal. Once initial access is gained, attackers can escalate privileges to root through insecure IPC or syslog-ng configurations and maintain persistence via unauthorized account creation, putting downstream managed environments at risk.

meta.rationale: Focus on servers identified as N-central appliances. Prioritize those running versions below 2026.4.1.26.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has exploited N-central vulnerabilities to gain a beachhead as the nable service account and is now attempting to escalate to root by tampering with syslog configurations or creating unauthorized local accounts.

hunt.name: Post-Compromise Escalation and Persistence on N-central
hunt.description: This hunt focuses on the 'Able2Shell' post-exploitation lifecycle on N-able N-central appliances. It follows an exposure flow, identifying vulnerable N-central instances and then examining host-telemetry for privilege escalation and persistence tradecraft described in recent research. The hunt specifically monitors the nable service account for anomalous file modifications and shell execution, alongside auditing new local account creations that could indicate an attacker establishing a long-term presence on the RMM server.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(LOWER(package_name), 'n-central') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(package_name), 'ncentral') > 0) AND package_version < '{{vulnerable_build_threshold}}'
config.description: Identify hosts running N-central versions prior to the 2026.4.1.26 hotfix to scope the hunt to potentially exposed appliances.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames running outdated N-central software. None means the estate is already patched or N-central is not present.

primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames running outdated N-central software. None means the estate is already patched or N-central is not present.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, activity_name, COUNT(*) as changes, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_account_change WHERE activity_id = 1 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name ORDER BY changes ASC
config.description: Identify unauthorized account creation on appliances, which is a reported persistence method in the Able2Shell disclosure.
config.expected_signal: Newly created user accounts on N-central appliances. Unexpected usernames should be scrutinized for correlation with vulnerability disclosure dates.

config.objective: Decide whether the observed file modifications and account changes on vulnerable N-central hosts indicate an active compromise or unauthorized post-exploitation activity.

config.question: the agent verdict is malicious or suspicious for at least one host

config.description: Direct results to remediation tasks if any host is judged as compromised or highly suspicious.
Address confirmed exposure and suspicious behavioral findings.
config.instructions:
1. For hosts with malicious or suspicious verdicts, verify if the account creation or syslog modification was unauthorized.
2. Ensure all identified vulnerable N-central instances are upgraded to build 2026.4.1.26 or higher immediately.
3. Validate that Agents and Probes are scheduled for updates following the server patch.
